subject: Version shelving handoff and network drain / rollback rules for AcmeHealth private fleet

Subject: Private fleet maintenance window & short-notice shelving process

Hi Soojin,

We need to schedule a narrow maintenance window next week to apply a minor runtime patch to our private cluster (AcmeHealth VPC, region us-west-2). Legal needs the plan for version pinning (a temporary hold on the control-plane-driven upgrades) and the network drain/rollback criteria before they sign off.

Two specific asks:
- Can Redwood provide a one-page flow we can present to procurement that shows the handoff steps (who pins, who authorizes unpinning) and the expected downtime/impact?
- Our SREs want clear abort criteria for an emergency unpin/rollback during a maintenance window (we prefer quantified thresholds).

We have a contract milestone tied to this (deal A-3247), so procurement is on a short timeline.

Can you loop in the ops folks and share a proposed checklist?

Thanks —
Tom

Tom —

Thanks for the note. Attaching a concise starter pack (see attachments) and a suggested procedure below. Karthik and Laura are on the thread for ops/runbook validation.

High-level proposal (summary page for procurement):
- Pre-window: customer opens Maintenance Request in our shared Drive + HubSpot record (HUBSPOT-1245789). Redwood triages and confirms compatible model pins.
- Shelving / Pin: Customer requests a "shelve" action — we flip the version pin on the control-plane for the spec'd fleet and mark nodes read-only for model updates. Pin is acknowledged in the maintenance ticket by both parties.
- Drain: Begin graceful connection drain for non-sticky sessions; live traffic funnels to warmed canary nodes (if configured). Expected user-visible impact: small increase in p95 tail for 5–15 minutes during drain depending on workload.
- Patch / Verify: Apply patch to non-critical canary slice first (10% traffic), run smoke & eval set checks.
- Unpin / Rollout: If canary OK, progressively roll out. If not, follow rollback ladder below.

Abort / rollback criteria (proposed quantitative thresholds):
1) Error spike: sustained 5m error-rate > 2.0% (baseline 0.1–0.5%)
2) Latency regression: sustained 5m p95 > baseline + 700ms or absolute p95 > 1200ms
3) Semantic regressions: automated eval set drop >= 4% for key prompts or > 1% high-severity hallucination metric
4) Observability gaps: tracing/metrics missing for >10% of shards after 10 minutes

Rollback ladder (fast to slow):
- Immediate: Unplug new model variant and revert traffic to pinned image (control-plane command: redwood unpin --force <fleet>).
- Short-term: Reapply previous stable runtime build cluster-wide from snapshot.
- Fallback: Evacuate fleet to a non-affected availability group and freeze control-plane updates until post-mortem.

Attachments in this email: shelving-procedure-v1.pdf (one-pager), rollback-checklist.csv (operator checklist).

Karthik / Laura — can you validate the technical steps and add any required runbook steps (drill commands, expected time-to-recover)? I can produce a one-page procurement-ready PDF from this if we're aligned.

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Tom —

Updated per your asks. See the embedded changes below and attached runbook (runbook-shelving-v2.md). Short answers up front: 1) We can use a 3m sustained window for error-rate triggers; 2) Redwood will execute and validate the dry-run in your staging env (we'll need staging access + a short list of test prompts), 3) On-call escalation: Redwood will assign a direct dial-in and Zoom bridge for the 2-hour immediate window (details in the runbook). No SLA penalty for unilateral emergency unpin initiated by customer as long as the maintenance was requested and recorded in the shared ticket prior to the action; if unpin is done outside the agreed process we'll need a separate impact review.

Key edits (high level):
- Abort window changed to 3-min sustained metrics for error spike and latency regressions.
- Added dry-run ownership: Redwood ops to run "redwood shelve --dryrun --staging <acme-staging>" and verify rollback returns to pinned hash within 5 minutes. Customer to provide test prompts and a staging account role for the run.
- Added escalation contact: Redwood On-call (phone + zoom) + Redwood Solutions lead (Sooj in that window); details + rotation table in runbook-shelving-v2.md.
- Added explicit SLA note: Emergency unpin that prevents data loss or availability degradation will not incur SLA credit. We document the event and schedule a post-mortem.

Rollback steps (concise):
1) redwood unpin --force <fleet>  # instant revert to pinned images
2) if unpin fails: redwood rollback --snapshot <timestamp> --target <fleet>
3) if rollback fails: evict and re-route traffic to warm standby AZ (ops coordinate with AcmeNetwork).

Timeline estimate for the maintenance window (conservative):
- Prep & dry-run: 1–2 hours before window start
- Canaries + smoke: 15–30 minutes
- Progressive rollout (if green): 30–90 minutes depending on fleet size
- Post-window monitoring: 60 minutes

Next steps I propose:
1) Acme provides staging access and 4 representative prompts for the eval set.
2) Redwood schedules a 60m dry-run this week with Karthik / Laura present.
3) We finalize procurement one-pager and I will send an updated PDF to your procurement contact.

Attached: runbook-shelving-v2.md (includes escalation table and exact CLI commands).

Best,
